newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends weaker on slow steady selling.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends weaker on slow steady selling.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker at C$1.3894 (US$0.7173 on Wednesday from this morning's open of C$1.3876 (US$0.7206) on slow steady afternoon selling, dealers said.
* Analysts said the currency gave back all its gains from a morning rally and tumbled from midday strength around C$1.3851 (US$0.7219) in concert with a falling U.S. dollar.
Traders said the U.S. dollar tumbled amid market rumors that a newsletter from a Washington-based consultant said that the U.S. Treasury would support a stronger yen.
The U.S. dollar fell to 117.30 yen from Tuesday's close of 118.55 yen and slid to 1.6470 marks from 1.6930 marks.

Analysts said the Canadian dollar is also under pressure from speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve may hike interest rates. They said the currency remains weak ahead of the Federal Open Market Committe meeting on May 25 despite economic data which has not shown inflationary pressures rising in the United States.
On Wednesday, the U.S. Labor Department reported that the producer price index fell 0.6 percent in April, compared with expectations that it would remain unchanged.
Traders said they were looking to Thursday's U.S. consumer prices data for April.
A Reuter survey of economists forecast the April CPI will rise 0.1 percent.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar fell to 84.32 yen from Tuesday's close of 86.22 yen and firmed to 1.2190 marks from Tuesday's 1.2121 marks.
